forecasts.question: Will an Iranian official (Pezeshkian, Araghchi, or named Foreign Ministry spokesperson) make a public statement explicitly addressing the 14-point MOU on the record before EOD 2026-05-13?
forecasts.delta_reason: Carried forward as RESOLVED-AMBIGUOUS per prior session ruling. Horizon passed May 13; resolution status inherited from v44.1 graveyard.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named Iranian official (Pezeshkian, Araghchi, Baghaei, Larijani, or Mojtaba Khamenei) is quoted directly by name in Reuters/AP/AFP/IRNA/Press TV/Tasnim addressing the specific 14-point framework or its terms (not generic 'reviewing US proposals'). NO if only Pakistani-channel intermediaries comment publicly.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Direct quote in at least two of: Reuters, AP, AFP, IRNA, Press TV, Tasnim, or named-Iranian-official Telegram/X account. Anonymous 'sources' do not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If Iran issues a statement on US-Iran negotiations broadly but does not reference the 14-point framework specifically: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If Mojtaba addresses the question via written statement (no live address): counts as YES (named official, named question).

indicators.name: Tasnim publishes named Foreign Ministry comment on MOU
indicators.expected_effect: +25pp toward YES if observed; Tasnim is the IRGC-aligned outlet that broke the 14-point response May 2.

indicators.name: Mojtaba Khamenei live televised address
indicators.expected_effect: +30pp toward YES if observed in window; would also materially shift downstream forecasts toward de-escalation.

forecasts.question: Will a written US-Iran framework memorandum (the US-authored 14-point document delivered via Pakistan channel, or named successor) be confirmed signed by both parties before EOD 2026-05-18?
forecasts.delta_reason: No material movement. Araghchi flew from BRICS New Delhi (May 13-14) to Beijing, where he told Wang Yi Iran 'will only accept a fair and comprehensive agreement.' Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman declared on May 12 that war cessation and Hormuz unblocking are prerequisites to any nuclear discussions — functionally rejecting the US MOU sequencing. VP Vance stated May 13 that 'progress is being made' while acknowledging the nuclear red line has not been bridged. The enrichment moratorium gap (US ~20 years; Iran ~5 years) remains unbridged with three days to the May 18 horizon. Trump-Xi Beijing summit produced White House language that Hormuz 'must remain open' and Iran 'can never have a nuclear weapon,' but China's own readout omitted Iran and Xi reaffirmed continued Chinese oil purchases from Tehran. 0.07 reflects near-foreclosure of signed memo in remaining window.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named US administration official AND a named Iranian official publicly confirm signing of a written memorandum (the US-authored MOU/framework document delivered via Pakistan channel, or any named US-authored successor); OR if the document text is published by Axios/Reuters/State Dept with both parties acknowledging authenticity. Verbal or 'agreement in principle' without a document does not count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: At least two named official sources from each side, OR official document release by State Dept / Iranian Foreign Ministry / Pakistani Foreign Office acting as confirmed mediator. Reuters/AP/AFP/Axios reporting acceptable when both sides quoted by name.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If a memo is signed but Iran publicly disputes key terms within 72 hours: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO (per JCPOA-2022 failure pattern). If signed by envoys but not publicly confirmed by principals (Trump/Pezeshkian) by horizon: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Chinese-brokered framework without direct US-Iran bilateral named-official confirmation = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: Witkoff or named US envoy holds direct-channel meeting with Araghchi or named Iranian deputy
indicators.expected_effect: +10pp if confirmed; direct bilateral contact is a necessary condition for signing in the remaining 3-day window.

indicators.name: IRGC Quds Force statement endorsing diplomatic track
indicators.expected_effect: +15pp if observed; addresses the central JCPOA-2022 failure mode of envoys without IRGC sign-off.

forecasts.question: Will Iran formally and publicly reject the US-authored MOU/framework document (delivered via Pakistan channel) before EOD 2026-05-18?
forecasts.delta_reason: Small upward tick on elevated hardliner rhetoric. Kayhan editorial this week called Iran's counter-proposal 'reasonable and generous' while branding US demands 'complete surrender' — rejection-grade language at the hardliner outlet, now at PARTIAL indicator state. Iran FM spokesman Baghaei declared on May 12 that war cessation and Hormuz unblocking are 'prerequisites' to nuclear discussions, functionally rejecting the US MOU sequencing while avoiding the word 'rejection.' Araghchi at BRICS Delhi urged BRICS members to 'condemn US-Israeli unlawful aggression' — framing inconsistent with a leadership preparing to sign. Neither a named Araghchi statement explicitly rejecting the US-authored MOU text, nor a Mojtaba written statement, nor a Kayhan editorial using the specific document's language has been confirmed in tier-1 sources, keeping formal rejection below the resolution threshold. +4pp reflects hardliner rhetoric elevation without formal resolution.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Iran's Foreign Ministry, Pezeshkian, or Khamenei's office issues a public statement using rejection language (rad, mardud, rejected, refused) specifically naming the US-authored MOU/framework document delivered via Pakistan channel. NO if Iran continues 'reviewing' or issues a counter-proposal without explicit rejection of the US document.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Direct attributed quote in at least one of: Reuters, AP, AFP, Haaretz, Times of Israel — carrying named-Iranian-official attribution. Iranian state media alone (IRNA, Press TV, Tasnim, Fars) does not satisfy this rule without tier-1 corroboration.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Counter-proposal with modifications = NOT rejection (resolve NO). Walk-away from talks without explicit rejection statement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Iran describing US terms as unacceptable in general without naming the specific document = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: Kayhan editorial uses rejection-grade language explicitly naming the US MOU document
indicators.expected_effect: +10pp toward YES if elevated to OBSERVED with tier-1 corroboration; currently PARTIAL: rejection rhetoric present, explicit MOU-document-naming not confirmed in tier-1 text.

indicators.name: Mojtaba Khamenei written statement against US framework
indicators.expected_effect: +25pp toward YES; supreme leader family rejection is the canonical signal and would push p toward 0.55+.

forecasts.question: Will IDF conduct a second airstrike on Beirut (within the Beirut governorate) before EOD 2026-05-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. Horizon expired May 15. The last confirmed IDF strike inside Beirut governorate (Dahiyeh/Haret Hreik) occurred May 6, killing Radwan Force commander Ahmad Ghaleb Ballout — that event predates the forecast window. On May 13, IDF drone strikes hit the coastal highway at Jiyeh and Barja, approximately 20km south of Beirut per AP, Reuters, and Lebanese Health Ministry — placing them in Mount Lebanon governorate, not Beirut governorate. Per the ambiguity rule ('Drone strike on Beirut outskirts [Mount Lebanon governorate] = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO'), this resolves NO. No tier-1 source reported a Beirut-governorate strike on May 14 or May 15. Israel-Lebanon third-round talks ongoing in Washington May 14-15 provided diplomatic-restraint context. Resolution: RESOLVED-NO.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if any Israeli airstrike or named operation hits a location within Beirut governorate borders. Southern Lebanon strikes outside Beirut governorate do NOT count. Reported by Lebanese Health Ministry OR Reuters/AP/AFP OR IDF spokesperson.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Lebanese government sources or major wire confirming impact location within Beirut governorate; OR IDF spokesperson statement naming Beirut as target.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Drone strike on Beirut outskirts (Mount Lebanon governorate) = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO unless explicitly described as 'Beirut strike' by IDF or Lebanese government. Intercepted strike that did not impact = NO.

indicators.name: Hezbollah rocket fire from south of Litani at more than 20/day rate
indicators.expected_effect: OBSERVED (IDF reports >40/day); did not produce Beirut-governorate IDF retaliation within forecast window.

indicators.name: Smotrich public threat to bolt over Iran-deal terms
indicators.expected_effect: Not observed; absence consistent with NO resolution.

forecasts.question: Will Saudi Arabia publicly restore US access to Prince Sultan Air Base airspace for CENTCOM operations before EOD 2026-05-25?
forecasts.delta_reason: Reduced from 0.28 to 0.15 on structural-disincentive analysis. WSJ reported ~May 8 (unnamed US officials) that Saudi Arabia and Kuwait lifted restrictions on US military basing and overflight, restoring Prince Sultan Air Base access operationally. F5's resolution criteria require a named DoD source in Reuters/Bloomberg/Times of Israel OR a Saudi MOFA statement. Seven days of silence since operational restoration (May 8-15) with no named-source public confirmation is evidence that the silence is deliberate: Saudi Arabia has strong domestic-audience incentives against publicly hosting US military operations against a Muslim-majority neighboring state, and the Pentagon appears content with quiet operational cooperation. MBS-Trump second phone call (~May 7-8) confirmed bilateral warmth but produced no public statement on Prince Sultan access. ADS-B tanker tracks not yet confirmed by tier-1 source. Ten days remain, but the structural disincentive for public announcement is assessed as the dominant factor. Judge sets p=0.15, retaining residual for a scenario in which the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire talks produce a broader Gulf announcement creating a window for public Saudi confirmation.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if KC-46 tanker tracks resume over Saudi Arabia airspace AND Saudi MOFA or Pentagon issues public statement confirming restored access. ADS-B tracking alone = AMBIGUOUS (could be exception). NO if airspace remains closed past 2026-05-25 OR if access is partial/conditional with public Saudi reservation.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Pentagon named spokesperson + Saudi MOFA statement; OR Reuters/Bloomberg/Times of Israel confirming sustained access with named DoD source. ADS-B alone is supportive but not resolving. Unnamed US officials do not satisfy resolution criteria.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Partial access (e.g. tankers but not strike aircraft) = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Trump claims access restored without Saudi named-official confirmation = NO. Operational access confirmed by unnamed officials only = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: MBS-Trump phone call or in-person summit
indicators.expected_effect: OBSERVED (~May 7-8, second call). Bilateral warmth established; did not produce public statement on Prince Sultan access.

indicators.name: ADS-B tanker tracks return to Saudi airspace confirmed by tier-1 source
indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES if confirmed by tier-1 source; operational return precedes public announcement.

indicators.name: Pentagon press briefing or defense.gov statement confirming KC-46 operational access from Prince Sultan
indicators.expected_effect: +35pp toward YES; named DoD statement would satisfy resolution criteria directly.

forecasts.question: Will at least 50 commercial vessels per day transit the Strait of Hormuz during any consecutive 7-day window before EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: Reduced from 0.18 to 0.09. Transit data as of May 14 shows only 6 vessels/day versus the 50-vessel resolution threshold — an 88% shortfall. Lloyd's war-risk premiums remain at approximately 2.5% of hull value, 67% above the 1.5% indicator trigger. Trump-Xi Beijing summit produced a White House joint statement that the Strait 'must remain open'; however, the Chinese government's own readout omitted any mention of Iran, Xi simultaneously reaffirmed continued Chinese oil purchases from Tehran, and no operational commitment by either party was announced. Xi stated these positions publicly; they represent diplomatic language without operational implementation. Araghchi at BRICS Delhi reiterated Hormuz reopening is conditioned on war cessation. Neither resolving indicator (Lloyd's below 1.5%, major shipping line announcement) shows movement. 26 days remain but the gap between current operational state and resolution threshold is now so large — requiring war cessation or ceasefire, insurer confidence recovery, and commercial return — that probability above 0.09 would require a sudden ceasefire-and-deal scenario not currently forecast above 22% on the most optimistic track.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Hormuz Strait Monitor (primary), Lloyd's List Intelligence (secondary), or UNCTAD reports an average of at least 50 daily commercial transits over 7 consecutive days within the horizon window, using Western-insured vessels (dark fleet excluded per ambiguity rule).
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Hormuz Strait Monitor (primary), Lloyd's List Intelligence (secondary), UNCTAD Maritime Trade report (lagging confirmation). At least one of these three sources must confirm the 7-consecutive-day average.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If only Iranian-flagged or sanctions-evading dark-fleet vessels make up the transit count but Western insurers still refuse coverage: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. The operationally meaningful question is whether Western commercial shipping has returned. Extortion-toll dark-fleet traversal does not count toward YES.

indicators.name: Lloyd's war-risk premium reduced below 1.5% of hull value
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; insurance is the binding constraint on Western commercial transit. Current ~2.5%.

indicators.name: Maersk/MSC/Frontline announce return to scheduled Hormuz transit
indicators.expected_effect: +25pp toward YES; major shipping lines lead the resumption and signal insurer coverage secured.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's governing coalition lose its 61-seat Knesset majority (via defection, dissolution motion, or no-confidence) before the mandatory 2026-10-27 election date?
forecasts.delta_reason: No material movement — Friday weekly cadence, no intra-week probability delta permitted per standing rule (Codex DA #12). New ambiguity rule added per Judge hygiene fix to cover the voluntary dissolution scenario. Seat count verification flagged for Sunday review: if Degel HaTorah departure alone pushed coalition below 61, F7 may already qualify as RESOLVED-YES independent of the dissolution bill timeline.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats by defection or vote failure), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel confirmation. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: counts as YES (majority lost). If a single party (e.g. Smotrich) departs but coalition retains 61+: counts as NO. Coalition submitting a voluntary dissolution bill while nominally retaining 61+ seats = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO for F7, pending seat-count verification at time of Knesset vote; F7 resolves YES only on confirmed loss of 61-seat majority by defection or vote failure, not on administrative dissolution scheduling. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas allowed per Codex DA #12.

forecasts.question: Will the Knesset dissolution bill pass a preliminary (first-reading) vote before EOD 2026-05-28?
forecasts.delta_reason: Raised from 0.72 to 0.82 on multi-faction co-sponsorship confirmation and identified vote window. Times of Israel confirmed May 15 that the earliest preliminary vote can occur is Wednesday May 20 per Knesset procedural rules. All four coalition factions — Likud, Shas, UTJ including Degel HaTorah, and Religious Zionism/Otzma Yehudit — co-sponsored the dissolution bill, fulfilling the primary indicator condition. Multiple opposition parties (Yesh Atid, Yisrael Beytenu, Democrats, Ra'am) submitted parallel dissolution bills, reinforcing procedural pressure on Speaker Ohana to schedule the vote within the May 20-28 window. Judge sets 0.82, retaining residual for scenarios in which Speaker Ohana delays beyond May 28 due to diplomatic emergency, legal challenge, or sudden coalition defection that changes vote arithmetic.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Knesset Speaker schedules and conducts a preliminary (first-reading) vote on the coalition dissolution bill, and the bill passes, before EOD 2026-05-28.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Times of Israel/Haaretz/Reuters confirmation of the vote result.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Procedural postponement beyond May 28 without a vote = NO (horizon-based). If Ohana schedules the vote for May 28 but it is delayed by quorum failure: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO pending a rescheduled vote within 24 hours. Opposition bill passing instead of coalition bill = YES if the effect is the same (dissolution vote passes).

indicators.name: All four coalition factions present and voting for first reading
indicators.expected_effect: OBSERVED: all four co-signed the bill as of May 13-14. This was the primary indicator; its observation is the main driver of the 0.72 to 0.82 move.

forecasts.question: Will the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire (expiring EOD 2026-05-18) be formally extended or replaced by a new agreed framework before or on 2026-05-19?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial seed. Third round of US-mediated Washington talks ongoing May 14-15; multiple outlets report 'cautious optimism' for extension without reporting a breakthrough. Lebanon's delegation demands a permanent ceasefire and full Israeli withdrawal timeline; Israel insists on freedom of operations until Hezbollah military capacity is resolved. Neither party has announced readiness to accept the other's core position. Structural pressure for extension is high — neither the US, Lebanon, nor Israel has a stated interest in full ceasefire lapse during the fragile Iran-US negotiation phase. p=0.68 reflects the high base rate for ceasefire extensions in active negotiations discounted for the real structural disagreement on permanent terms.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if US mediators, Lebanese government, OR Israeli government publicly confirm a ceasefire extension or new truce agreement before EOD May 19. NO if ceasefire lapses without confirmed extension.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: US State Department named official OR Lebanese PM/MOFA OR IDF spokesperson via Reuters/AP/AFP.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Unilateral Israeli 'operational pause' without Lebanese acknowledgment = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Lebanese statement without Israeli confirmation = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Extension of fewer than 72 hours described as 'temporary halt' without bilateral agreement language = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: Third-round Washington talks produce agreed text before May 15 close of business
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES if observed; agreed text by COB May 15 would make formal announcement before May 19 nearly certain.
